transcription.text: Hi. For those who've been watching for a long time, and I mean like more than a decade, you might remember EEVBlog number 50.
Well, you won't remember the actual number, but you might remember the Cree-led thermal design video, which was, well, only gotten 50,000 views over like the last 11 years or whatever.
So, not that impressive, but I think it's a really good video going into thermal heatsink design.
And I actually used a clip of that in my like ancient, my 10-year-old intro video, which I have to update.
Anyway, those who remember that video might remember these homemade, obviously, Cree LED strips that I made.
I know they look crusty now, but they looked shiny as almost like 11 years ago now.
And these are for my outdoor deck.
And, you know, LED lighting wasn't like as ubiquitous.
And, you know, LED lighting wasn't as ubiquitous then as it is now.
And really, you know, you couldn't buy like the LED strips and things like you can these days.
So, I made up my own using Cree, what were state-of-the-art at the time, Cree XPG LEDs here.
And I stuck them down into a big aluminium plate here, none of that aluminium rubbish, and with some thermal adhesive here to act as a gigantic heatsink.
And I did lots of whiteboard calculations and all sorts of stuff about, you know, generic.
So, the video was more about that than it was about installing these LEDs.
But anyway, these have been up on my back deck.
They were like up on beams on my back deck, then shining upwards from the beam, and then rebounding off the white roof, and then, you know, coming down.
It was designed to look all funky, and it did.
It was really quite nice.
And I've had the, and the reason that I put them on really thin strips like this is so that you couldn't, from the ground, you couldn't see them.
The lights just magically turned on.
Ta-da!
And, like, as if they're coming out of the beams, or something like that.
Um, so, yeah, and, and they've been in there for, um, 11 years.
I just took them out, and I noticed that, like, a couple of years ago, um, like, some LEDs started to fail.
So, they lasted probably about seven, eight years, something like that, like, fully exposed like this.
I did not, uh, like, coat these in anything.
I just used, soldered them on, put the thermal adhesive down, I just used some, um, I think I tacked, yeah.
Did I tack these down, or something?
Maybe with some hot snot, or something.
